messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: High error rate spike for tenant-prod-42. Alert: 40% 5xx over last 3m. Likely routing/fallback policy misconfig. initial_ts=1769804321

matt (oncall): on it. getting briefed. what's the customer impact?

lara (cust-success): multiple customers on that tenant reporting timeouts and 503s in the last 10m. two enterprise customers (Acct A, Acct B) have opened tickets.

jin (eng-ops): seeing a lot of requests being routed to hosted-pool instead of dedicated-pool for tenant-prod-42. logs show policy eval picked hosted variant as fallback repeatedly. possible spillover misroute.

miriam (runtime): hmm. query: did we recently change routing weights or add a new model-variant alias? I see a canary for model-x-8q that maps to hosted-only.

alex (sre): pile of evidence in the runtime logs:
```
[1769804300] route_eval tenant=tenant-prod-42 preferred=tier=dedicated allowed_pools=[dedicated-eu, dedicated-us] fallback_pools=[hosted-eu] decision=hosted-eu reason=capacity-tier-mismatch
[1769804312] kvcache-miss
[1769804315] fallback-loop-detected: asking to reroute to eu-west-1 -> eu-west-1 (same)
```

matt (oncall): fallback-loop-detected line worries me. could be policy referencing region alias that resolves back to hosted pool. immediate mitigation: block hosted-eu from accepting requests for tenant-prod-42. can someone push a quick deny rule?

jin (eng-ops): I can push temporary ACL. executing: `rbacctl update-route --tenant tenant-prod-42 --deny-pool hosted-eu --reason "incident 1769804321"`

deploy-bot: deploy started for config-change rbacl-1769804321 by jin

miriam (runtime): while that deploy goes, let's stop automatic spillover for capacity-tier. change policy: `spillover.enabled=false` for that tenant so we don't get cross-tier routing until we fix mapping.

jin (eng-ops): applied spillover disable: `api patch /routing/tenants/tenant-prod-42 {"spillover":false}` - responses 200.

alex (sre): confirm logs show routing decisions now marked `deny-hosted` for that tenant. error rate started to drop but still elevated (down from 40% to ~12%).

lara (cust-success): pinging customers. letting Acct A know we applied temporary mitigation and will follow up on root cause. they asked if this was a config change on our side — they want a timeline.

miriam (runtime): debug note: the fallback rule `(region:europe) -> pool:hosted-eu` had an old alias `region:europe` which resolves to both dedicated-eu and hosted-eu. but our policy evaluation order used alias expansion incorrectly and ended up preferring hosted-eu because of a stale weight. looks like a regression from the policy refactor yesterday.

matt (oncall): ok that's the root cause hypothesis: alias expansion + stale weight => hosted chosen => spillover loop because region fallback points back to same pool. next steps: revert policy refactor changes for alias expansion, and add a guard to prevent alias resolving to pools with different capacity-tier. can we do a rollback?

jin (eng-ops): starting rollback of policy-refactor commit `c8f9a2`. `git revert --no-commit c8f9a2 && deploy-manifest --env prod`. deploy-bot: queued.

deploy-bot: rollback deploy started for routing-service at 1769804400

alex (sre): while rollback runs, add a validation rule in the router to reject policy configs that map the same alias to both hosted and dedicated. quick patch I can push: `routerctl validate-alias --alias region:europe --reject-cross-tier`

miriam (runtime): +1. that will prevent recurrence. also will add an emergency metric alert if alias expansion changes more than N pools.

lara (cust-success): customers acknowledged the interim mitigation, asking ETA for full fix. can we commit to 60m?

matt (oncall): aim for 60m. keep comms every 15m. after rollback finishes, we'll test with canary traffic to tenant-prod-42.

(10m pass)

deploy-bot: rollback deploy completed at 1769804660. status: success.

jin (eng-ops): rollback confirmed. policy-refactor reverted. reloading routing configs.

alex (sre): re-run routing unit-tests: all pass locally. spinning up small canary: `trafficctl route --tenant tenant-prod-42 --percent 1` to dedicated-eu.

miriam (runtime): canary traffic looks good. no fallback to hosted pool. monitoring shows 5xxs for tenant-prod-42 down to baseline ~0.5%.

lara (cust-success): telling customers we rolled back and did canary checks, next update in 30m with RCA.

matt (oncall): good. next permanent tasks: (1) add alias cross-tier validation, (2) add unit test for alias expansion with tier checks, (3) postmortem and config review, (4) ensure tenancy metadata can't be overwritten by hosted-only model aliases. assign owners?

jin (eng-ops): I'll own (1) and (2).

miriam (runtime): I'll own (4) and help with the postmortem.

alex (sre): I'll draft the postmortem and timeline. include the customer impact and mitigation steps.

lara (cust-success): I'll coordinate customer comms and the follow-up notes to Acct A and Acct B.

deploy-bot: scheduled follow-up deploy for alias validation at 1769810000 (manual approval required).

matt (oncall): handing off to night on-call at 1769804987. night on-call please monitor the routing metrics for tenant-prod-42 for the next 4 hours. tagging @oncall-night in the incident system.

incident-bot: incident severity set to P1. ticket created: INC-2026-832. link: https://tickets.example.internal/INC-2026-832

lara (cust-success): adding summary to the ticket: "Routing policy alias expansion regression caused hosted pool to be preferred for tenant-prod-42, triggering capacity-tier spillover and fallback loop. Mitigated by temporary deny rule and policy rollback. Customers notified."

matt (oncall): closing slack coordination thread, keep updates in the ticket and postmortem doc. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
